record.title: Jiangsu publishes provincial subsidies for AI compute, corpus and model development
record.summary: A Jiangsu provincial cyberspace office page posted October 9 reproduces a five-agency notice dated September 30 that sets three support schemes for eligible organizations: compute/token vouchers covering up to 50% of qualifying service spending with a CNY 5 million per-entity ceiling; corpus vouchers supporting qualifying data and corpus purchases at up to 50% with a CNY 1 million ceiling, alongside separate support for dataset construction and embodied-robot data collection; and model vouchers covering 30% of qualifying model R&D spending up to CNY 1 million. The official notice page appeared on the provincial cyberspace office site on October 9. These are written eligibility and payment rules, not evidence that funds have been allocated, claimed or paid, or that the measures changed AI activity.
organizations: Jiangsu Provincial Development and Reform Commission
Cyberspace Affairs Office of the CPC Jiangsu Provincial Committee
Jiangsu Department of Industry and Information Technology

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A notice signed September 30 by five Jiangsu provincial agencies issues implementation schemes for token/compute vouchers, corpus vouchers and model vouchers; the provincial cyberspace office page displays a publication time of October 9.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The token-voucher scheme provides eligible Jiangsu users support for qualifying intelligent-compute purchases of at least CNY 10,000; provincial and city support combined is ordinarily capped at 50% of actual payment and CNY 5 million per entity, subject to local schemes and provincial budget control.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The corpus scheme sets up to 50% support and a CNY 1 million per-entity cap for eligible corpus/data purchases, up to CNY 500,000 for qualifying national high-quality dataset projects or CNY 200,000 for provincial projects, and up to 30% support with a cumulative CNY 2 million cap for embodied-robot data collection transactions through the provincial data exchange.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The model-voucher scheme provides 30% of qualifying model R&D spending, capped at CNY 1 million, and ranks applications using registered-user, API-call and realized-contract indicators.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The policy text does not establish total appropriation, actual claims, disbursements, uptake or effects on AI activity.

evidence_gaps.description: The notice specifies rules but does not establish city budgets, applications, awards or expenditure under any of the three schemes.
No counterfactual or measured change in compute use, corpus transactions, model development, embodied-robot data collection or firm location was reported.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, three linked subsidy mechanisms could change marginal compute, corpus, embodied-data collection and model R&D costs for eligible Jiangsu organizations, a meaningful regional AI-industrial policy signal. The consequence is notable locally, but budgets, uptake and outcomes are not yet measured.
limitations: The notice is dated September 30, while the official web page displays an October 9 posting timestamp; these dates are kept separate.
No aggregate funding budget or city-level rollout plan was included in the opened notice page.
No applications, awards, payments, audit outcomes, beneficiary counts or economic effects were inspected.
The support schemes are regional and apply only to eligible entities and expenditures; national or province-wide effects cannot be inferred from their issuance.

A September 2, 2026 Hangzhou Binjiang policy already specified compute, model-token and corpus support; the Jiangsu notice should be read as a provincial package with distinct written terms, including embodied-robot data-collection support, not as the first local AI voucher program. Neither notice establishes actual uptake or effects.

brief.summary: A Jiangsu provincial cyberspace office page posted October 9 reproduces a five-agency notice dated September 30 that sets three support schemes for eligible organizations: compute/token vouchers covering up to 50% of qualifying service spending with a CNY 5 million per-entity ceiling; corpus vouchers supporting qualifying data and corpus purchases at up to 50% with a CNY 1 million ceiling, alongside separate support for dataset construction and embodied-robot data collection; and model vouchers covering 30% of qualifying model R&D spending up to CNY 1 million. The official notice page appeared on the provincial cyberspace office site on October 9. technical.claimed_result: The issuing agencies frame the package as a way to support Jiangsu AI innovation and mobilize fiscal funds; no resulting innovation or economic growth is demonstrated.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official Chinese notice sets the three schemes, eligibility conditions, ceilings, reimbursement formulas and reporting/payment procedures. It does not show funding totals or actual implementation.
technical.implementation_status: Written scheme issued September 30, 2026; official provincial web posting displayed October 9, 2026. Compute and corpus support is subject to city proposals, provincial budget control and later settlement; model support uses application review and ranking. Actual grants were not inspected.
technical.mechanism: A provincial fiscal support package reimburses portions of eligible compute-service consumption, qualifying corpus/dataset acquisition or development, embodied-robot data-collection transactions, and model R&D. City governments define local rates within provincial ceilings for compute/corpus support; the provincial government provides budgeted reimbursement and conducts later settlement/audit.
technical.regime: Eligible enterprises, universities, research institutions and other specified entities operating in Jiangsu, with different requirements for compute services, data/corpus transactions, embodied-robot data projects and already-filed large-model services.
technical.reproducibility: The notice and three scheme texts can be checked on the official provincial website; all amounts and eligibility statements above are drawn from the listed sections.
technical.strongest_baseline: A Hangzhou Binjiang notice published September 2, 2026 specifies municipal compute vouchers at 30% (up to 60% for priority computing resources) with a CNY 20 million ceiling, model-token use support up to CNY 10 million, and corpus support up to 30% capped at CNY 2 million per year. This is an announced municipal comparison, not evidence of awards or effects; Jiangsu’s notice is a provincial package and additionally sets out embodied-robot data-collection transaction support.

brief.title: Jiangsu publishes provincial subsidies for AI compute, corpus and model development
brief.why_it_matters: The package targets three input costs for AI activity in one major Chinese province: compute, data and model development. If local budgets and uptake are substantial, it could change marginal costs for eligible research institutions, companies and individual business entities and provide a concrete regional policy design to compare with other compute and data subsidies. The notice does not state a total appropriation or show uptake or economic effects.
